absent: Full type definitions and remaining fields for compaction control, zone, node, free area, page, allocation context and capture control beyond members observed in use.

Implementations of pageblock address and alignment helpers, offline range skipping, isolation suitability predicates, block isolation, cached cursor updates, scanner meeting tests, restart and reset helpers, watermark checks, reclaimable accounting, zone bounds, population tests, mobility derivation, gap sizing, explicit trigger detection, scan limit computation, freelist reordering, skip flag access, emptiness tests, fallback tables, migration callbacks, tracing, node lock primitives and contiguous statistics collection.
Complete behavior of the zone compaction main loop beyond the truncated partial fragment, including drain handling, rescan paths and final return paths.

Concrete numeric values and meanings for allocation orders, migration types, compaction results, isolation outcomes, fallback outcomes, zone counts, page state counters, watermark selectors and allocation flags.
Wiring, units, permissions and side effects for the proactiveness, fragmentation threshold, unevictable allowance and explicit trigger tunables.
Lock ordering, interrupt context requirements and sleep versus atomic constraints beyond the observed zone lock pairing and node thread lock pairing.
Scope of contiguous allocator fallback, definition of defragmentation mode and scheduling of background versus direct compaction.
Error handling for out of memory, signal delivery timing and contention propagation to callers outside the visible override.

findings.text: The proactive compaction aggressiveness control defaults to twenty on a zero to one hundred scale, where larger values lower the fragmentation score required to trigger background work.
The external fragmentation threshold tunable is initialized to five hundred.
The allowance for compacting unevictable pages is initialized from the build configuration default rather than from a fixed literal in the visible fragment.
An explicit compaction trigger control exists as a separate integer tunable without a fixed literal default shown in the visible fragment.

The fast start cache retains the smallest frame number observed so far. A maximum sentinel disables recording, an initial zero adopts the first observation, and later observations only lower the stored value.

Consumption of the cached fast start value is one shot. Unset or sentinel leaves the migration cursor unchanged, otherwise the cursor is replaced by the cached value and the cache is returned to the disabled sentinel.

Fast migration block search is skipped and the current migration cursor is reused when skip hints are ignored, when the current block must be finished, when resuming away from a zone or block start, for request orders at or below the costly threshold, and for direct non movable requests smaller than a pageblock.

When enabled, fast search examines only movable freelists for orders below the request and at or above the costly threshold, bounded by a scan limit and confined to the nearer portion of the scanner gap. Recently skipped blocks are ignored, examined entries are moved to the tail, the lowest free frame seen is recorded, examinations count toward the migration scan total, and failure increments a failure counter before falling back to the cached cursor.

Freelist examination during fast search is performed while holding the zone lock with interrupts saved, releasing it with the prior interrupt state restored. Cursor arithmetic outside the list walk is not covered by that critical section.

Migration isolation scans whole blocks from the fast search start up to the free scanner, clamped to block and zone boundaries. Offline ranges are skipped, very long zones yield the processor at intervals, recently failed blocks are not retried except after a successful fast find, unsuitable sources update the cached cursor and are skipped, and a block isolation contention aborts the attempt.
Isolation mode includes unevictable pages only when the corresponding allowance is enabled, and requests asynchronous migration whenever the control mode is not synchronous.
Observation of the per node reclaim thread pointer together with its running state is performed atomically under the node reclaim thread lock, with the boolean outcome returned after release.

External fragmentation for a given order is zero when no free pages exist. Otherwise it is the percentage of free pages outside suitable blocks, computed as one hundred times free pages minus suitable blocks scaled by order size, divided by total free pages from contiguous page statistics.

Zone fragmentation is external fragmentation at huge page order. The weighted zone score scales that value by present pages over node present pages plus one. The node score is the sum of weighted scores for populated zones only.

Proactive watermarks derive from the aggressiveness control as one hundred minus the control value for the low mark, with a leeway of at most ten or half the low mark added for the high mark capped at one hundred. A node qualifies only when the control is nonzero, the reclaim thread is idle, and the node score exceeds the high mark.

Termination is decided in order. Meeting scanners ends the run as complete for whole zone work and partial skipped otherwise, with cached positions reset and a block skip flush flagged for direct requests. Proactive runs stop for reclaim activity and otherwise continue while the zone score exceeds the low mark. Explicit trigger requests and mid block cursors always continue. Defragmentation mode for background work succeeds on high watermark satisfaction. Direct requests succeed when a free page of the needed type, contiguous allocator fallback for movable, or stealable fallback exists at or above the order. Contention or a fatal signal overrides other outcomes with a contended result.

Whole block claiming is attempted when the order covers a full pageblock or at least half of one, for reclaimable or unmovable requests regardless of size, and whenever mobility grouping is disabled. Other small movable requests only borrow temporarily to avoid lasting pollution.

Fallback suitability first rejects requests that should not claim and empty areas. It then walks the ordered fallback table for the requested mobility excluding the last category, reporting found with the selected type when any candidate list is nonempty and empty otherwise.

The zonelist suitability check determines whether any zone in the allocation context could benefit from compaction. It honors processor set eligibility, estimates availability as reclaimable pages scaled down by order plus snapshotted free pages, and tests each candidate against its minimum watermark.

Per zone allocation suitability succeeds immediately when watermarks are already met, using block counted free pages in defragmentation mode for background work and ordinary free pages otherwise. Costly asynchronous requests without contiguous allocator permission are skipped when low order watermarks plus a gap cannot be met. Zones failing the general suitability test are skipped and the remainder are approved to continue.

Zone compaction initializes scan totals and page lists, derives the target mobility from the allocation mask, bypasses initial suitability for explicit trigger requests, clears stale skip information on retry, and seeds migration and free cursors to zone extremes for whole zone work or to cached positions clamped inside the zone with promotion to whole zone when starting at the beginning.

The compaction loop calls an external drain helper once and then repeats termination testing, pageblock completion marking on revisits, migration candidate isolation with release on contention, migration of isolated pages with success accounting, conversion of out of memory without scanner meeting into contention, and forced completion of partially scanned blocks after failed asynchronous work to allow skip marking.

The compaction control carries migration and free cursors with a fast start cache and failure counter, request order and mobility with allocation flags and masks, synchronous versus asynchronous mode with direct, proactive and whole zone selectors, a zone pointer with highest index, scan totals with isolated page counts and per order free lists plus a migration list, and contention with pageblock completion flags.

Zones expose a start frame with end derived bounds, present page counts, free areas indexed by order, a protecting lock, cached migration cursors for synchronous and asynchronous work with an initial value and a free cursor, a block skip flush flag, and a back pointer to the owning node. Nodes expose per zone arrays, a reclaim thread pointer, and total present pages.
Each buddy free area tracks a total free count and per mobility freelists whose entries link through the page buddy linkage and support emptiness queries and tail reordering during scans.
The external fragmentation query for a zone and order is provided for callers outside the defining file.
The zonelist suitability test for compaction is provided for allocation and reclaim callers outside the defining file.
Linear scans over very large zones may traverse many unsuitable blocks, so the isolation path yields the processor at regular block intervals to avoid monopolizing the processor.

Fast search reorders freelist entries under lock but avoids moving entries on the recently skipped path because safe traversal assumes removal rather than reordering, so reordering there could corrupt iteration.
A pending fatal signal or observed contention forces a contended termination even when a suitable page exists, so success of the search does not guarantee that allocation will proceed.
Proactive compaction is suppressed while the per node reclaim thread is running, preventing concurrent reclaim and compaction from competing over the same node.
Requests marked as via the explicit trigger bypass initial suitability screening and force the finish decision to continue rather than succeeding early.
The public finish check traces the internal termination decision and maps the no suitable page outcome to a request to continue scanning, leaving all other results unchanged.
